verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe an Amazon SES SMTP interface that SMTP-enabled languages and software can connect to, offered as an alternative to the SDK and API. They also cover routing an existing email server's outgoing mail through SES, which fits the legacy-app case. None of the evidence covers how SMTP credentials are generated or handled, so that part of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: documentation of generated SMTP credentials, SMTP endpoint/port/TLS details, independent hands-on corroboration of SMTP relay use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send through a documented SMTP relay with generated credentials when my framework or legacy app can't call the REST API

citations.quote: You can send email through Amazon SES by using a variety of SMTP-enabled programming languages and software to connect to the Amazon SES SMTP interface.
To configure your existing email server to send all of your outgoing mail through Amazon SES, see Integrating Amazon SES with your existing email server.
You can send email from Amazon EC2 by using an AWS SDK, by using the Amazon SES SMTP interface, or by making calls directly to the Amazon SES API.
